description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/helpers.rs:128-132.

    pub(crate) fn iso8601_before(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
        let a_sec = &a[..a.len().min(19)];
        let b_sec = &b[..b.len().min(19)];
        a_sec < b_sec
    }

The byte-index slice &a[..N] requires N to be a UTF-8 char boundary. If input has a multi-byte character (≥2 bytes) intersecting byte index 19, the slice panics.

Current call sites:
- space.rs:1321: invite expiry, expires_at is UTCDate (validated 20-char ASCII)
- space.rs:1408: same (different context but same fact)
- message.rs:408: sender expiry, expires_at is UTCDate (validated)
All current callers pass UTCDate-derived strings which are guaranteed 20-char ASCII per the UTCDate validation in jmap-types::id.rs:165-197. So the panic is currently unreachable.

But:
1. JMAP-x2gd.7 documents that two sites (message.rs:355 sentAt, position.rs:163 lastReadAt) wrap client-supplied strings via UTCDate::from (no validation). If those values are ever passed to iso8601_before in the future, the panic becomes reachable.
2. The function is a public-via-crate helper (pub(crate)). A future contributor reading the signature ('takes &str') has no way to know it requires ASCII-only input.

Fix: defense-in-depth, accept either non-ASCII without panicking. Two options:
(a) Use .get(..19).unwrap_or(a) — silently truncates on non-boundary.
(b) Use .chars().take(19).collect::<String>() — semantically correct but allocates.
(c) Take &UTCDate instead of &str — types enforce the precondition.

(c) is the workspace-idiomatic fix; the function's only callers already have UTCDate-typed values.

Trade-off: this is currently a 'theoretical issue with no plausible trigger' under the workspace test-and-call-site invariants. If JMAP-x2gd.7 is closed first, this becomes pure defense-in-depth. Labeled P3 accordingly.
title: helpers::iso8601_before uses byte-index str slicing; non-ASCII input panics. Defense-in-depth on validated-only call sites.
